root.note: Further back it may come from an Indo-European root meaning ‘to ferment’. That step is only probable.

history: Queso and English cheese are the same word. Both start from Latin cāseus. In Spain the sounds swapped places and merged, roughly caseu, caisu, queisu, queso. Germanic peoples borrowed the word from Latin, and that line ends in English cheese and German Käse. So why do French fromage and Italian formaggio look so different? They come from another Latin word, formaticus, ‘made in a mould’. Italian still has cacio from cāseus too. Portuguese queijo stays close to Spanish. So if you know English, you already half know this Spanish word.
historyEinfach: Queso comes from the Latin word cāseus. English cheese and German Käse come from the same Latin word. The sounds changed a lot over time. French says fromage and Italian says formaggio. These words come from a different Latin word. It meant ‘made in a mould’. Cheese was pressed into a shape.

elsewhere.text: Wiktionary calls cheese and queso doublets: two words from one Latin word.
French named cheese after its mould. Italian does the same with formaggio.
German Käse is the same Latin word, borrowed long ago.
